title: The Digestive System
seo_title: Year 4 Science: The Digestive System Worksheets (Mouth, Stomach and Intestines)
standard_text: Describe the simple functions of the basic parts of the digestive system in humans.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on the digestive system: the mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestines and rectum, the journey of food, and digestion models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Food is broken down on a long journey.
key_sub: Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum.
body_html:
How to think about it

The digestive system breaks food down so the body can use it.

  • Mouth (teeth chew, saliva softens) → oesophagus → stomach (acid and churning) → small intestine (nutrients into the blood) → large intestine (water taken back) → rectum.
  • Food passes quickly down the oesophagus but stays for hours in the stomach and intestines.
Example

Food leaves the stomach. Where next?

Stomach → small intestine

Answer: the small intestine

Example

Stomach 3 h, small intestine 4 h, large intestine 20 h. Total?

3 + 4 + 20

Answer: 27 hours

Common mistakes

  • Thinking food goes down the windpipe.
  • Thinking digestion only happens in the stomach.
  • Thinking the large intestine is the longest part.

faq.q: What are the parts of the digestive system?
faq.a: The mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and rectum. Each has its own job in breaking down food.

faq.q: What does the small intestine do?
faq.a: It finishes digesting food, and nutrients pass through its thin walls into the blood.
Usually between one and three days from eating to waste leaving the body, with most of the time spent in the intestines.
